transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As part of our standard launch-governance process for the October 1 external availability of our clinical documentation platform, I need each of you to state any legal condition that must be included in the launch packet before I can give final authorization. The packet currently uses our standard software, privacy, product-description, and enterprise-contract templates. Please go ahead and share any conditions or concerns from your functional areas.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag a blocking condition before final authorization. My completed license review of the production build found that module M-17 incorporates an AGPL-licensed library. Under our company's approved proprietary deployment policy, M-17 must be replaced before any external customer access is granted. I have not yet added this license-review result to the launch packet, and this remediation must be completed and documented before October 1.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Elena, I have a blocking condition from the privacy perspective. In the signed design-partner agreement, I confirmed that customer content may not be used to train or improve our models and must be deleted within exactly 30 days after account termination. However, I have not yet updated the standard privacy language in the launch packet to reflect these binding commitments. The privacy terms in the launch packet must be revised to match these contractual obligations before final authorization is granted.

transcript.text: Elena, I have a blocking condition from the regulatory perspective. My intended-use review concluded that the planned language describing automated clinical triage recommendations makes diagnostic claims. The launch materials must instead describe the product as an administrative workflow tool only. I have not yet circulated that review, and the product-description materials must be revised to remove all diagnostic-claim language and reframe the product as an administrative workflow tool before final authorization is granted.

I confirmed that the anchor hospital's signed letter of intent permits production use only after the company provides a SOC 2 Type II report and includes an annual customer audit right in the definitive agreement. I have not yet inserted those terms into the contract draft. The enterprise-contract terms in the launch packet must be revised to include the SOC 2 Type II report delivery requirement and the annual customer audit right before final authorization is granted.
